hero.title: Digital sovereignty for public administration
hero.lead: Digitalising public administration requires technology that is both powerful and meets the highest standards of security and independence.

intro: Artificial intelligence is becoming a fixed part of modern administrative processes. Yet many AI services run on non-European clouds — with consequences for data protection, security, and the ability to act.

The Centre for Digital Sovereignty (ZenDiS) has defined clear criteria that a digital solution must meet to offer the highest degree of digital sovereignty. Synaplan was built precisely to these standards.

risksSection.title: Five risks of non-European cloud and AI services
risksSection.lead: ZenDiS describes these risks when using non-European services. With Synaplan they can be substantially reduced — without giving up technical innovation.

risks.title: 1. Extraterritorial legal access
risks.text: Data-protection uncertainty caused by foreign authorities accessing personal data.

risks.title: 2. No control over code and data
risks.text: Limited information security when source code and data are neither inspectable nor controllable.

risks.title: 3. Technological lock-in
risks.text: Inflexibility due to missing exit options and dependence on individual vendors.

risks.title: 4. Uncontrollable costs
risks.text: Rising license fees for cloud-based SaaS models with no spending cap.

risks.title: 5. Externally driven innovation
risks.text: Dependence on the proprietary development cycles of global vendors.

next.title: The open source answer
next.text: Synaplan addresses these risks systematically — through consistent open source development within the European ecosystem.

hero.title: Sovereignty through open source
hero.lead: Synaplan meets the ZenDiS criteria for digital sovereignty — inspectable, adaptable, and developed in the European community.

intro: The Centre for Digital Sovereignty (ZenDiS) has defined five requirements for a digital solution to offer the highest degree of digital sovereignty. Synaplan meets these criteria.
Here is how we put the strict ZenDiS requirements into practice.

criteriaSection.title: Five criteria — five answers from Synaplan
criteriaSection.lead: Every ZenDiS requirement, translated into a concrete Synaplan promise.

criteria.title: Maximum data protection: lawful and GDPR-compliant
criteria.requirement: Lawful operation without the risk of access by foreign authorities.
criteria.promise: Synaplan can be operated fully GDPR-compliant in your own systems (on-premises) or in a secure, German cloud. Your sensitive administrative data is guaranteed to stay where it belongs — protected from access by third parties or foreign states.

criteria.title: Full freedom: no vendor lock-in
criteria.requirement: Ensuring the ability to switch, to prevent dependence on individual vendors.
criteria.promise: Synaplan relies on open standards. You can migrate data and processes at any time and keep the free choice of your IT service providers. Language models can be switched at any point — chat data, memories, and documents remain in your Synaplan instance.

criteria.title: Absolute sovereignty: full control over your AI system
criteria.requirement: Control and the ability to act — even in the event of outage, blocking, or a change of provider.
criteria.promise: Synaplan is yours. Even if conditions change or external systems fail, your AI solution remains fully operational. At no point are you dependent on the infrastructure of a single vendor.

criteria.title: Trust through transparency: inspectable source code
criteria.requirement: Transparency and traceability of the technology, e.g. through inspectable code.
criteria.promise: No “black box” for public administration: Synaplan's source code is available on public repositories (GitHub, Open CoDE) and how it works is fully traceable. This creates the verifiability the public sector needs.

criteria.title: Future-proof: developed in the European open source community
criteria.requirement: The solution can be adapted and shaped by the community or your own service providers.
criteria.promise: Synaplan grows with your requirements. As part of the European open source ecosystem, you benefit from continuous innovation and can adapt, extend, or have the solution tailored precisely by the IT service providers of your choice at any time.

openSource.conclusion: Synaplan combines state-of-the-art artificial intelligence with the values of digital sovereignty — secure, independent, and transparent.

intro: Synaplan is not an isolated tool but part of an open ecosystem. The AI can be used where your staff already work — and at the same time run entirely within your own infrastructure.
This keeps the path from the email all the way to the language model consistently in European, sovereign hands.

hero.title: About Synaplan & contact
hero.lead: We support public administration in the digitally sovereign use of AI.

about: Synaplan is an open source AI knowledge platform that combines artificial intelligence with the values of digital sovereignty: data protection, transparency, and independence.

Developed within the European open source ecosystem, Synaplan enables on-premises operation with local models as well as the flexible connection of external language models — depending on protection needs and task.
Synaplan is maintained by metadist and the community and is freely available on public repositories.
contact.founder: Behind Synaplan stands metadist data management GmbH — the company vehicle of founder and internet pioneer <ralf>Ralf Schwöbel</ralf>, who has significantly shaped the German internet since the late 1990s: in government advisory boards as well as in numerous open source projects.
contact.advisor: The German technology executive <nemat>Claudia Nemat</nemat> supports the sovereign software-architecture approach as an advisory board member and shareholder, advocating for a free, open (open source) and stable infrastructure.

trust.minutesLead: The hosted platform is web.synaplan.com. The operator is metadist data management GmbH in Düsseldorf.

avv.title: Data processing agreement
avv.lead: On the hosted platform the customer is the controller and metadist is the processor.
avv.draft: The text below is the template of 6 November 2026. Management has not countersigned it. The company record names no data protection officer. It does not replace a signed contract.
points: It covers web.synaplan.com. It does not automatically cover an installation you run yourself.
It names the subject, the data, the people, the instructions, deletion, and the subprocessor list.
avv.language: The other languages on this page explain the template. The signature copy is the German text.
avv.ask: Ask for the copy to sign

clauses.title: 1. Parteien
clauses.body: Auftraggeber ist die Stelle, die Synaplan gehostet nutzt. Auftragnehmerin ist die metadist data management GmbH, Königsallee 82, 40212 Düsseldorf, Deutschland.

clauses.title: 2. Gegenstand und Dauer
clauses.body: Gegenstand ist der Betrieb der gehosteten Plattform unter web.synaplan.com für den Auftraggeber. Der Vertrag gilt für die Laufzeit des Nutzungsvertrags und endet mit ihm.

clauses.title: 3. Art und Zweck
clauses.body: Die Auftragnehmerin stellt die Plattform bereit: Konten, Gespräche, Dateien, Wissenssuche, das Website-Widget und die Kanäle, die der Auftraggeber selbst einschaltet.

clauses.title: 4. Art der Daten
clauses.body: Kontaktdaten der Nutzerinnen und Nutzer, Inhalte von Gesprächen, hochgeladene Dateien, Nutzungsdaten und Abrechnungsdaten.

clauses.title: 5. Betroffene Personen
clauses.body: Beschäftigte des Auftraggebers und Personen, die das Widget oder einen vom Auftraggeber eingeschalteten Kanal nutzen.

clauses.title: 6. Weisungen
clauses.body: Verarbeitet wird nur auf Weisung. Weisung sind dieser Vertrag und die Einstellungen im Konto. Eine Weisung, die gegen Recht verstößt, wird nicht ausgeführt. Die Auftragnehmerin sagt das dem Auftraggeber.

clauses.title: 7. Vertraulichkeit
clauses.body: Personen, die Daten sehen, sind zur Vertraulichkeit verpflichtet. Das gilt für Beschäftigte der Auftragnehmerin und für Personen bei einem Unterauftragnehmer, soweit sie diese Daten sehen.

clauses.title: 8. Sicherheit
clauses.body: Die Schutzmaßnahmen sind die TOMs auf dieser Seite, mit dem dort genannten Stand. Die Auftragnehmerin behauptet keine Maßnahme, die dort nicht steht.

clauses.title: 9. Unterauftragnehmer
clauses.body: Die Unterauftragnehmer stehen in der Liste auf dieser Seite. Ein neuer Name wird auf der Seite veröffentlicht, bevor er Daten sieht. Der Auftraggeber kann widersprechen. Dann suchen beide eine andere Lösung oder beenden den Vertrag. Die Auftragnehmerin bleibt für die Pflichten eines Unterauftragnehmers verantwortlich.

clauses.title: 10. Rechte der betroffenen Personen
clauses.body: Die Auftragnehmerin hilft bei Auskunft, Berichtigung, Löschung und Export. Dafür gibt es Funktionen in der Software. Was die Software nicht kann, beantwortet sie auf Anfrage an privacy@synaplan.com.

clauses.title: 11. Löschung
clauses.body: Nach dem Ende des Vertrags werden die Kontodaten gelöscht, soweit kein Gesetz das Aufbewahren verlangt. Der Auftraggeber kann vorher exportieren. Auf Anfrage bestätigt die Auftragnehmerin die Löschung schriftlich.

clauses.title: 12. Nachweis
clauses.body: Auf Anfrage beschreibt die Auftragnehmerin die TOMs. Ein Audit vor Ort wird verabredet und sieht keine Daten anderer Kunden.

clauses.title: 13. Ort der Verarbeitung
clauses.body: Die gehostete Plattform steht in Deutschland. Ein Gespräch verlässt die EU nur, wenn der Auftraggeber ein Modell einschaltet, das außerhalb der EU antwortet. Das Einschalten ist seine Weisung.

clauses.title: 14. Eigenbetrieb
clauses.body: Betreibt der Auftraggeber Synaplan selbst, ist die metadist data management GmbH nicht Auftragsverarbeiterin der Inhalte. Sieht ihr Personal im Support in das System, braucht das einen eigenen kurzen Vertrag.

clauses.title: 15. Verletzung des Schutzes
clauses.body: Stellt die Auftragnehmerin eine Verletzung des Schutzes personenbezogener Daten fest, informiert sie den Auftraggeber ohne schuldhaftes Zögern. Soweit bekannt, nennt sie die Art der Verletzung, die ungefähre Zahl der betroffenen Personen und Datensätze, die wahrscheinlichen Folgen und die ergriffenen Maßnahmen. So kann der Auftraggeber seine Frist von 72 Stunden einhalten.

clauses.title: 16. Folgenabschätzung
clauses.body: Braucht der Auftraggeber eine Datenschutz-Folgenabschätzung oder eine Konsultation der Aufsichtsbehörde, gibt die Auftragnehmerin die Informationen, die sie über diese Verarbeitung hat.

toms.title: Safeguards
toms.lead: These are the measures we can show for the hosted service. Article 32 GDPR.

items.title: Encrypted connection
items.text: The website and the platform are served over HTTPS. The privacy policy says the same.

items.title: Location Germany
items.text: The hosted platform runs on Hetzner servers in Germany. Cloudflare sits in front, for delivery and protection.

items.title: Database on three servers
items.text: The database is kept in step across three servers. If one stops, the others keep serving.

items.title: Operator access
items.text: Operators sign in with a key. The usual SSH port 22 is closed.

items.title: A log inside the product
items.text: The software keeps an audit log for 365 days unless that value is changed. Deleting an account goes through the product's deletion path.

items.title: No training
items.text: Chat and file content is not used to train models.

limits: There is no external pentest yet, no ISO 27001 certificate, and no BSI C5 attestation.
The container images are not signed yet, and we do not publish an SBOM yet.
We do not claim encrypted disks, and we do not claim a second copy of every search index.
Management has not countersigned this list. The company record names no data protection officer.

processors.title: Subprocessors
processors.lead: These parties see data of the hosted platform or of the websites. A cloud model is in the list only for the answer that selected it.

rows.name: Hetzner Online GmbH
rows.role: Provides the servers for the website and the hosted platform.

rows.name: Cloudflare Germany GmbH
rows.role: Delivers the sites and filters attacks. Sees connection data.

rows.name: Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL
rows.role: Sends account mail through Amazon SES in eu-west-1. Sees the address and the mail we send, not the chats.

rows.name: Stripe
rows.role: Takes payment when someone pays for a hosted plan. Sees payment data, not the chats.

rows.name: The selected model
rows.role: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and Groq are in the USA. Mistral is in the EU. A local model such as Ollama stays on the server. The text of an answer goes only to the model selected for it.
rows.trains: Synaplan does not train. Whether the model provider stores the API call is in that provider's contract. We do not promise zero retention at the provider.

rows.name: Google
rows.role: Only when someone signs in with Google. Sees the sign-in, not the chats.

rows.name: Meta (WhatsApp) and Telegram
rows.role: Only when the customer turns that channel on. Messages on that channel also pass through that service.
rows.trains: Synaplan does not train. The channel provider has its own rules.

flow.title: Where a chat goes
flow.lead: Three paths. The installation and the selected model decide which one applies.

paths.title: Hosted, local model
paths.text: The answer is produced on the servers in Germany. The text is not sent to a model provider.

paths.title: Hosted, cloud model
paths.text: Synaplan stores the chat in Germany and sends the text needed for that answer to that one provider. Other providers do not see it.

paths.title: You run it
paths.text: The content stays in the customer's installation. metadist sees it only when the customer explicitly gives us access for support.

flow.doc: Technical note in the source repository

aiAct.title: AI Act
aiAct.lead: Synaplan is the software an organisation uses to deploy AI. Synaplan is not the company that trains the model. The organisation that runs Synaplan for its people is the deployer.
does: Mail, WhatsApp, Telegram and the website widget say that an AI is answering.
A generated image, audio file or video keeps a mark from the model provider. When signing is on, Synaplan signs the file as well.
The page “Using AI well” explains in ten short sections what a model can and cannot do. An organisation can ask its people to read it once. Nobody is locked out.
deployer: Say, in its own channels, who is responsible for the assistant.
Decide which data may be pasted into a chat.
Keep a person in the loop before a draft is sent, published or filed.

security.title: Security and AI incidents
security.lead: A software weakness and an AI incident are two different reports.
security.vuln: Please do not describe a weakness in public. The private report is on GitHub. We confirm it within three working days. If you cannot use GitHub, write to privacy@synaplan.com and put the details only in the reply.
security.incident: An AI incident means: the assistant discloses data it should not, a generated file is marked in a way that misleads people, or an answer causes harm that the deployer reports to us. Mail privacy@synaplan.com with the subject “AI incident”. We reply within 24 hours and say what happened, who is affected, and what we changed. If the first reply is not enough, reply with the word escalation. The management of metadist data management GmbH then sees the report.
security.doc: Security policy in the source repository

availability.title: Availability
availability.lead: This is the commitment for the hosted platform. A service credit belongs in the offer, not on this page.
items: Target: 99.5 percent in a calendar month for web.synaplan.com, excluding announced maintenance.
We announce maintenance at least 14 days ahead, outside Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 18:00 (Europe/Berlin).
Support replies within one working day.
Whether web.synaplan.com answers right now is on the status page. We do not publish a measured monthly history.
If you run Synaplan yourself, availability is yours.

access.title: Accessibility
access.lead: The target is WCAG 2.1 AA, and with it BITV 2.0. A finished BITV audit does not exist yet.
items: The product rules require enough contrast for text and for large text.
Known gap: there is no published BITV 2.0 test report.
Report a barrier on this page or in the software to privacy@synaplan.com. We reply within one working day.

open.title: What is still missing
open.lead: Tenders often ask for these. We do not have them yet.
items: External pentest: planned for the first quarter of 2027, not commissioned yet.
ISO 27001 and BSI C5: not in place.
Signed images and an SBOM: planned, not published.
Measured availability over months: not published. The status page only shows whether the service answers right now.
